prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: In this downward-angled egocentric view inside a store, the depth map highlights the camera wearer's hands and held item at the bottom center of Frame 1 as the brightest, nearest surfaces (~0.3–0.5 m away, within arm's reach), clearly closer than the flat floor (~1.0–1.5 m) and the top-edge background (~1.5–2.0 m) containing a floor stand on the left, a mirror in the center, a small shoe-and-tie shelf on the right, and another person's lower leg and white shoe ~0.3 m right of the shelf (~1.2–1.5 m away). Across Frames 2 to 5, as the camera wearer tilts further down and turns right—causing the background shelf and the other person's feet (whose upper body, face, and gaze direction are entirely cropped out above the frame) to retreat out of the top-right corner—the foreground red shopping basket filled with clothes at the bottom center (~0.4–0.6 m away, within arm's reach) and a black metal rack base to its right (~0.5–0.8 m away, ~0.2 m from the basket) remain bright and elevated above the darker floor. The depth map makes it easier than RGB alone to perceive the 3D height of the piled clothing, basket rim, and tubular rack legs relative to the grey floor beneath them, as well as the recessed cubbies of the white shelf in Frame 1. However, the map is unreliable in Frame 4, where a severe illumination-like artifact makes the flat floor appear bright/near on the left and pitch black/far on the right, and in Frames 2–4, where the other person's white shoes at the top-right edge blend indistinguishably into the floor depth.
descriptions.segmentation: Across the five downward-looking frames, the segmentation map leaves the store floor, background mirror and shelf (~1.5–2.0 m ahead), black clothing rack base (~0.5–0.8 m away on the bottom right), and the other person's lower legs and white shoes at the top-right edge (~1.2–1.5 m away, facing roughly leftward with their upper body and head out of view) completely unsegmented. In Frame 1, it detects only the foreground cluster within the camera wearer's arm's reach (~0.3–0.5 m away at the bottom center), rendering a pink `person` mask over the wearer's two hands and wrists alongside two smaller overlapping `cell phone` masks (~0.1 m apart) on the left cuff area and central held item. As the wearer turns right and looks down at the red shopping basket and clothing across Frames 2, 3, and 4 (~0.4–0.6 m away), the map is entirely blank, before reappearing in Frame 5 to segment the dark blue folded garment resting on top of the basket at the bottom center (~0.4–0.6 m away, within arm's reach) as a teal `backpack` mask. Compared to RGB alone, the masks in Frames 1 and 5 sharply delineate the outer silhouette of the wearer's hands and the top clothing bundle against the underlying basket and floor. However, the map is highly unreliable, missing all scene furniture, the red basket, and the nearby person across every frame, while falsely labeling part of the wearer's left wrist/garment as a second `cell phone` in Frame 1 and misclassifying the folded clothes in Frame 5 as a `backpack`.
descriptions.pose: In this top-down egocentric sequence, the pose map detects a magenta left-hand skeleton in the bottom-left foreground of Frame 1 (~0.3–0.4 m from the camera wearer, within arm's reach), showing the wrist on the left and fingers extending rightward toward the held object and the unmapped right hand (~0.1 m to the right). Throughout all five frames, no pose keypoints are detected for the other person whose lower leg and white shoes appear ~1.2–1.5 m away near the right and top-right edges in Frames 1–4 (~0.3 m from the white shelf, with their torso and head cropped out of view as they retreat out of the frame), because only their feet and ankles enter the field of view. As the camera wearer turns right and carries the red basket of clothes at the bottom center (~0.4–0.6 m away, within arm's reach) beside the black metal rack base on the bottom right (~0.5–0.8 m away), Frames 2, 3, and 5 remain completely black, while Frame 4 shows a tiny vertical yellow body-skeleton fragment on the red basket's clothing at the bottom center (~0.5 m away). What the pose map provides beyond the RGB image is the precise finger joint alignment and palm orientation of the motion-blurred left hand in Frame 1. It is unreliable elsewhere, failing to detect the camera wearer's right hand in Frame 1, the hand gripping the basket in Frame 3, or the other person's lower limbs in Frames 1–4, while hallucinating a false-positive yellow body skeleton on the folded plaid garment in Frame 4.
